full_original_page:
# 843. Unknotting number and genus of positive fibered knots

**Area:** Geometric topology and knot theory
**Status:** 🟡 PARTIAL
**Last checked:** 2026-10-30

## Problem statement

Let $`K\subset S^3`$ be a smooth knot. Suppose that $`K`$ admits an oriented diagram with every crossing positive and that its exterior fibers over $`S^1`$, with a Seifert surface as fiber. Must
```math
u(K)=g(K)?
```


Here $`g(K)`$ is the minimum genus of a connected compact orientable surface embedded in $`S^3`$ with boundary $`K`$. The unknotting number $`u(K)`$ is minimized over **all diagrams** and crossing-change sequences, allowing isotopy between changes. Positivity is a property of the knot, rather than a prescribed diagram.

## Application

This asks whether a geometric surface invariant determines the minimum crossing-change complexity throughout the class of positive fibered knots. It extends a known equality for closures of positive braids.

## Known progress

The lower bound $`u(K)\ge g(K)`$ is known in this class. Kegel and collaborators obstruct three approaches to proving the opposite bound. Their Theorem 1.5 concerns the crossings of a particular genus-seven knot diagram: that diagram needs nine changes. The unrestricted value nine is separately proposed in Conjecture 1.6, rather than proved. Thus their diagram theorem does not settle the question above.

## References

1. M. Kegel, L. Lewark, N. Manikandan, F. Misev, L. Mousseau and M. Silvero, *On unknotting fibered positive knots and braids*, [accepted arXiv version 2312.07339v2](https://arxiv.org/html/2312.07339v2), Conjectures 1.1 and 1.6 and Theorem 1.5. *Annali della Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa, Classe di Scienze* **27**(3) (2026), 1499–1517, [doi:10.2422/2036-2145.202401_001](https://doi.org/10.2422/2036-2145.202401_001).
2. R. İ. Baykur, R. C. Kirby and D. Ruberman (eds.), *K3: A New Problem List in Low-Dimensional Topology*, Mathematical Surveys and Monographs **295**, AMS, 2026, Problem 1.5(a), [author copy](https://math.berkeley.edu/sites/default/files/surv-295-ruberman-watermarked-author-pdf.pdf), physical p. 14.

## Status review


**Known cases:** The latest accepted Kegel et al. text was reread: Theorem 1.5 is a fixed-diagram obstruction, and Conjecture 1.6 separately proposes that the unrestricted unknotting number is nine. A secondary disproof label is not supported by the primary theorem; general u=g remains unmatched.

**Remaining target:** Resolve the full Problem statement with its stated quantifiers and hypotheses; the restricted advances discussed here do not settle that target.
